newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close shade up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close shade up in thin trade.

text.p: The Philippine equities market finished slightly up on Tuesday as shares continued to move sideways, traders said.
"Market is going through a short term sideways behaviour. Investors are buying cautiously but the trend is quite positive," said Harry Liu, president of Summit Securities.
The main index was up by 5.62 points, or 0.18 percent, closing at 3,101.36 points.
Gainers slightly outnumbered losers 58 to 56 with 75 issues unchanged. Volume was at 2.2 billion pesos.
The rise in San Miguel and Petron Corp issues compensated for the drop in property counters like Filinvest Development and Filinvest Land.

The market will likely persist in its sideways movement with an upward bias as investors position ahead for 1997, Norman Cruz, trader at Philippine Asia Equity Securities Inc said. - KATHERINE ESPINA 63 2 841-8937 Fax 8176267
